analyzed_vuln.description: `ReflexHash::init` does not reject finite polygon coordinates whose derived bounds width/height overflows to infinity. For this PoV, the Y span overflows to `+inf`; initialization nevertheless succeeds because the grid-count expression becomes zero and `fGridConversion.fY` becomes zero, both considered finite. Later `ReflexHash::hash` evaluates an overflowing coordinate delta times that zero conversion (`inf * 0`), producing NaN; conversion to `int` yields an invalid large negative grid index. `ReflexHash::add` then accesses `fGrid[index]` out of bounds, and `SkTInternalLList::addToTail` crashes while operating on that invalid list object. Initialization must validate finite/non-overflowed bounds dimensions (and derived hash coordinates/indices) before allowing the hash to be used.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: The harness decodes this PoV as an 11-vertex polygon. Its finite float coordinates include Y values near `-2.128e38` and `+2.128e38`, so `setBoundsCheck` accepts the points but `bounds.height()` overflows to infinity. The polygon has nonzero winding and at least one vertex classified reflex, causing initial classification in `SkTriangulateSimplePolygon` to call `ReflexHash::add`. The malformed grid conversion then produces an out-of-range negative hash index. More generally, trigger requires at least three finite points, nonzero winding, an extreme coordinate span that overflows a bounds dimension while `ReflexHash::init` still passes, and a reflex vertex whose normalized coordinate calculation becomes NaN/invalid.

args: Analyze the vulnerability in ReflexHash::init/hash/add in skia/src/utils/SkPolyUtils.cpp. Explain the exact arithmetic failure, all callers and how init failure is handled, and recommend a minimal robust fix that validates overflowed bounds and ensures hash indices stay in range without changing normal polygon triangulation behavior.

The reported PoV reaches SkTriangulateSimplePolygon with 11 finite vertices, including Y near -2.128e38 and +2.128e38. SkRect::setBoundsCheck accepts each finite point, but bounds.height() overflows to +infinity. ReflexHash::init currently succeeds because derived grid count/conversion happen to be finite (zero), then hash computes an overflowing delta multiplied by zero, yielding NaN and an invalid negative integer index. ReflexHash::add indexes fGrid out of bounds and crashes in SkTInternalLList::addToTail. We need edit only C/C++ under skia, root-cause fix, and preserve intended behavior.
